neighbours.label: the start of the complement after an importance or necessity predicate in research prose ('it is of great importance to understand how ...'), peaking on the wh-word or verb that names what must be studied
fire: For public health, it is essential to understand why the infection returns.
It is therefore crucial to determine whether the effect lasts.
In this field it is of great interest to learn how cells repair damage.
So it is all the more important to find out which patients benefit.
It is vital to establish how quickly the toxin is cleared.
Clearly, it is necessary to examine why some trials fail.
It is of real importance to know when the symptoms first appear.
Thus it is critical to understand how the drug reaches the brain.
quiet: For public health, the essential work happens in local clinics.
The crucial result was published in a short letter.
In this field there is great interest among young researchers.
The importance of the trial grew after the first report.
Vital signs were recorded every hour by the nurses.
Clearly, the necessary equipment arrived late.
Its real importance was not recognised for decades.
The critical paper was cited thousands of times.

predictions: the wh-word or verb after 'important/essential to' 0.3-0.6; mentions of importance with no complement below 0.1
notes: Card: ' to' in 'of great interest to study', 'all the more important to select', ' that' after 'establish', ' can' after 'treatments which'. Probe: only 'of great importance to understand how the virus spreads' fired (0.668 at ' how'); 'want to establish that' 0.035, 'strategies for prevention' 0.021, 'which can slow' 0.025, 'The importance of the virus was unclear' 0.021. The test therefore uses the importance-to-understand frame only.
